ms.promise:
・We will implement a way of defining compound types in the Milestone 1 library.
・This implementation will use Boehm-Berrarducci encodings to be compatible with the Milestone 1 type system.
・We will add support for base functors to enable later work on elimination forms together with Turner totality.
・Specification of encodings (SOP and Data) for compound data types as part of their definitions will be included. There will also be a selection of different strategies for Data encodings.
・We will implement all the compound data types required by the Plutus ledger, specifically its V3.
・We will add tests to ensure that the type system from Milestone 1 behaves correctly on all Plutus primitive operations and on the ledger data types.
・These extensions to the Milestone 1 library will be documented as Haddocks.
・The CI from Milestone 1 will be extended to run the tests specified in point 3.
・We will publish the extended library on Hackage as an update.
ms.criteria:
・Milestone 1 library has gained the ability to define compound types
・Boehm-Berrarducci encodings are being used for compatibility with the Milestone 1 type system. 
・Base functors are supported. 
・Encodings for data types (both SOP and Data) can be specified. Furthermore, different strategies for Data encodings have been implemented.
・All compound data types required by the V3 Plutus ledger API exist in the Milestone 1 library.
・Tests for Criterion 1 and 2 functionality exist and pass, for both the Plutus primitive operations and ledger data types.
・Haddocks exist documenting all extensions t

ms.promise:
・We will extend the Milestone 1 and 2 library to support both introducing (creating) and eliminating (pattern matching and folding) values in the Covenant ASG.
・Folding will use recursion schemes, specifically catamorphisms.
・Base functors for existing compound recursive types, as well as Integer and ByteString Plutus core types, will be included.
・We will add tests to ensure that these forms behave correctly, by way of ASG construction (that is, 'end-to-end').
・We will document these extensions as Haddocks.
・The CI from Milestones 1 and 2 will be extended to run the tests specified in point 2.
・We will publish the extended library on Hackage as an update.
ms.criteria:

・A recursion scheme elimination form exists and uses catamorphisms.
・Base functors for existing compound recursive types, as well as Integer and ByteString exist.
・Tests using ASG construction have been added for the functionality of this Milestone, and pass.
・Haddock documentation exists for the public-facing new functionality added in this Milestone.
・The CI from Milestones 1 and 2 runs the new tests added in this Milestone successfully.
・The extended library has been published on Hackage as an update.

ms.promise:
・We will define c2uplc: an executable that translates the Covenant serial form as specified in Milestone 4 into serialized UPLC.
・We will use the conformance cases from Milestone 4 to verify that c2uplc works correctly.
・c2uplc will have a CLI, with instructions for use.
・Final close-out report
・Final closeout video
ms.criteria:
・An executable for generating UPLC from Covenant's serial form exists. Due to its dependence on Plutus, this can be in a separate repository from the rest of Covenant.
・The executable accepts a path to a Covenant serial form.
・The executable, when given a valid Covenant serial form, emits valid UPLC, whose execution semantics match those intended by the Covenant serial form.
・The executable, when given an invalid Covenant serial form, does not perform a translation. Instead, it errors with a clear and appropriate message.
・All the Milestone 4 conformance cases translate correctly using the exe
ms.report:
A. Output: A c2uplc executable that translatres Covenant to UPLC
Acceptance criteria: The executable generates UPLC from Covenant; accepts a path to a Covenant serail form; outputted UPLC execution semantics match those intended by the Covenant serial form; executable does not perform a translation on invalid Covenant. Note: a note on how to build the executable has been added to the README (Run `cabal build exe:c2uplc` to build it. To run it, use `cabal exec c2uplc`)
